1.

Ms. Saloni Mathur, Advocate has filed her power, today in the Court, on behalf of the applicant,
which is taken on record.
2.  Dr. S.B. Maurya, learned AGA-I for the State apprised the Court that on 25.09.2022 notice has been served upon the informant.
Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

3. Heard Ms. Saloni Mathur, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr. S.B. Maurya, learned AGA-I for the State.
4. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 04 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Mauranipur, District Jhansi during pendency of the trial.

sentences.text: FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant under Section 366 IPC and according to the FIR applicant enticed away the minor daughter of the informant aged about 14 years.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant in the FIR is totally false and baseless and actually daughter of the informant is major girl aged about more than 18 years and she according to her own wish had gone along with applicant and this fact is evident from her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C.

She further submits that at the time of recording the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. prosecutrix also provided her high school mark-sheet and according to high school mark-sheet her date of birth is 05.07.2004, therefore, at the time of incident she was around 17 years and 8 months old,
therefore, she was at the verge of majority.
She further submits that in the present matter applicant is in jail since 29.03.2022 i.e. for more than one year.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that in the FIR informant disclosed the age of the victim as 14 years but could not dispute the fact that according to high school certificate the age of victim was 17 years and 8 months and she did not make any allegation against the applicant.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Considering the fact that even as per high school certificate of the prosecutrix she was at the verge of majority and she did not make any allegation against the applicant in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. rather in her both the statements she stated that she had gone along with applicant on her own and thereafter performed marriage with him, in my view, applicant, who is in jail for more than one year, is entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant - Abhishek Alias Annu be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
